title: A 30–180 ms window raised path ratios by up to 8.04 percent in 500 passive chains at selected Allen time scales
abstract: We tested how a finite pulse window affects a steady passive path bound. Five time-constant quantiles from 280 selected Allen mouse inhibitory cells set time scales in synthetic three-cell chains. The conductances and cell combinations were assumed. With a 30–180 ms window, the largest path ratio was 1.068123 in 20 equal-cell cases and 1.080375 in a 500-case grid that permits unequal cells. Of the 500 ratios, 145 exceeded 1.01 and 18 exceeded 1.05. Independent time integration checked the largest ratio. The delayed-window short-time limit is 1.359809. This extends a published finite-window counterexample to the Allen analysis window. It does not show a passive failure in measured circuits. Intrinsic time constants are only illustrative model scales. No activity traces or actual three-cell fits were tested. Original code, proof, aggregate results, figure, source hashes and external regeneration steps are supplied.

display.caption: Synthetic passive chains can exceed the steady path bound with a 30–180 ms window. Shading marks selected Allen cell time scales; it does not show measured circuit ratios.

citations.reason: Extends its steady Allen path test to a delayed transient window.
Builds on its established finite-window counterexample. Adds a delayed-window formula and a benchmark at selected Allen time scales.
